observations: body L1-L6: the formulas are checked: they are rule (α) of p. 190 with sin vers P = R + R sin φ sin δ / (cos φ cos δ) and sin alt. merid. = cos (φ ∓ δ); with cos φ cos δ + sin φ sin δ = R cos (φ − δ) they give L4, and with the declination counted with its sign cos (φ ∓ δ) is cos (φ − δ), which cancels in L6.
body L1-L4, L6, L10, L19, L23, L25, L32, L33, L35: the minus signs are printed as long dashes (9.7 to 10.6 pt; that of L10 8.5 pt); they are set as minus signs.
body L9-L10: with the radius 1, sin h = sin φ sin δ + cos φ cos δ cos t gives L10.
body L15: the dash of «al-Battānī» measures 3.6 pt, a hyphen.
body L16: Nallino's addenda et emendanda (Part I, p. LXXIII) read «191,16, pro ortographicam l. orthographicam.»; the printed «ortographicam» is kept.

body L21-L26: the figure stands at the left of lines 21 to 26, which are set beside it in a narrow measure. It is the first figure of p. 190 drawn again with the perpendicular HZ, and is redrawn from measurements of the print: the meridian as a half circle over the horizon; the horizon, FL, HK, the parallel FG and the axis from C to the pole as straight lines (here FL, HK and the axis are printed solid); ZH in dashes, each dash where it printed; the brace φ along the arc; the bold italic letters and the word Polus.

body L21-L35: the proof is checked. In the triangle FZH the angle at Z is right and the angle at H equals XGC = 90° − φ, since HZ is parallel to the horizon; hence FZ : FH = cos φ : R. With FH = sin vers t FX / R (p. 190) and FX = cos δ, FZ = sin vers t cos δ cos φ / R², and FZ = FL − ZL = sin altit. merid. − sin h gives (I).
body L25: a spot of ink under the s of «cos δ» (the last of the line); it is not a sign.
body L30: a short upright stroke stands before the R under «cos φ»; it is not a sign.

lines.transcription: $\text{sin vers}\,t = \biggl(R + R\,\dfrac{\sin\text{φ} \sin\text{δ}}{\cos\text{φ} \cos\text{δ}}\biggr) - \dfrac{\sin h\,\biggl(R + R\,\dfrac{\sin\text{φ} \sin\text{δ}}{\cos\text{φ} \cos\text{δ}}\biggr)}{\cos (\text{φ} \mp \text{δ})}$

$= \dfrac{R\,(\cos\text{φ} \cos\text{δ} + \sin\text{φ} \sin\text{δ})}{\cos\text{φ} \cos\text{δ}} - \dfrac{R \sin h\,(\cos\text{φ} \cos\text{δ} + \sin\text{φ} \sin\text{δ})}{\cos\text{φ} \cos\text{δ} \cos (\text{φ} \mp \text{δ})}$.
Sed (ut e III capite patet) $\cos\text{φ} \cos\text{δ} + \sin\text{φ} \sin\text{δ} = R \cos (\text{φ} - \text{δ})$, ergo
$\text{sin vers}\,t = R^2\,\dfrac{\cos (\text{φ} - \text{δ})}{\cos\text{φ} \cos\text{δ}} - R^2\,\dfrac{\sin h \cos (\text{φ} - \text{δ})}{\cos\text{φ} \cos\text{δ} \cos (\text{φ} \mp \text{δ})}$,
et tandem
(I) $\text{sin vers}\,t = R^2\,\dfrac{\cos (\text{φ} - \text{δ}) - \sin h}{\cos\text{φ} \cos\text{δ}}$,

lines.tex: ergo $FZ = FH\,\dfrac{\cos\text{\textgreek{φ}}}{R}$. Vidimus supra $FH = \text{sin vers}\,t\,\dfrac{FX}{R} = \text{sin vers}\,t\,\dfrac{\cos\text{\textgreek{δ}}}{R}$; itaque
lines.transcription: ergo $FZ = FH\,\dfrac{\cos\text{φ}}{R}$. Vidimus supra $FH = \text{sin vers}\,t\,\dfrac{FX}{R} = \text{sin vers}\,t\,\dfrac{\cos\text{δ}}{R}$; itaque
$FZ = \dfrac{\text{sin vers}\,t \cos\text{δ}}{R} \times \dfrac{\cos\text{φ}}{R} = \dfrac{1}{R^2}\,\text{sin vers}\,t \cos\text{δ} \cos\text{φ}$.
Sed $FZ = \text{sin altit. merid.} - \sin h$; ergo
$\text{sin altit. merid.} - \sin h = \dfrac{1}{R^2}\,\text{sin vers}\,t \cos\text{δ} \cos\text{φ}$,
unde
$\text{sin vers}\,t = R^2\,\dfrac{\text{sin altit. merid.} - \sin h}{\cos\text{δ} \cos\text{φ}}$,
ut erat demonstrandum.
